content.definition: An algorithmic paradigm that solves complex problems by breaking them down into simpler subproblems, storing the results of subproblems to avoid computing the same results again.
core_principles: Optimal Substructure: Optimal solution contains optimal solutions to subproblems
Overlapping Subproblems: Same subproblems are solved multiple times
Memoization: Store results to avoid recomputation
Bottom-up Construction: Build solution from smaller to larger problems
when_to_use: Problems with recursive structure and overlapping subproblems

bottom_up_tabulation.description: Iterative approach building from base cases

linear_dp.description: 1D array, each state depends on previous states
linear_dp.complexity: Time: O(n), Space: O(n) or O(1)

grid_dp.complexity: Time: O(m*n), Space: O(m*n) or O(min(m,n))

knapsack_dp.complexity: Time: O(n*W), Space: O(n*W) or O(W)

1d_dp.python:
def solve_1d_dp(n):
    # Initialize DP array
    dp = [0] * (n + 1)
    
    # Base cases
    dp[0] = base_value_0
    if n > 0:
        dp[1] = base_value_1
    
    # Fill DP table
    for i in range(2, n + 1):
        dp[i] = recurrence_relation(dp, i)
    
    return dp[n]
